cards.subject: The Searing Blade
lines: The version most people picture is two redesigns later: Cho'gall, the Twilight's Hammer, Adarogg, Slagmaw. None of it is here.
In this one the cult is the Searing Blade and there are four names — Oggleflint, Taragaman the Hungerer, Jergosh the Invoker, Bazzalan.

cards.subject: You never leave Orgrimmar
lines: The way in is a portal in the city's own inner district, right beside Neeru Fireblade's tent.
It is the lowest-level dungeon in the game, and in practice Horde-only — no Alliance player has a route to the middle of a Horde capital.
There is a volcanic crack under the auction house and it is full of cultists.

cards.subject: Neeru Fireblade
cards.tag: The man who sends you in
lines: The orc warlock pointing Horde players down the hole is the secret leader of the Burning Blade, working the Shadow Council from inside the capital.
Thrall knows, and leaves him standing there in the open as a source.
Everyone who took his quest was being run by both sides at once.

cards.subject: No Alliance quests
lines: The whole quest apparatus down here is Horde: Thrall's chain, Neeru's chain, the Grimtotem satchel.
The corpse-running workarounds people remember are all later expansions.
It is the only dungeon in the game that half the playerbase has no reason to enter.

cards.subject: Two invasions, one hole
lines: The Ragefire troggs and their shamans came up from below, out of the lava tunnels. The earthborers and molten elementals are the chasm's own.
The Searing Blade cultists, enforcers and warlocks came down from Orgrimmar.
They are two separate infestations that happen to share a crack under a city.

cards.subject: Oggleflint
lines: The trogg chieftain is not on the way to anything. He sits down a side branch, and groups pushing for the bosses walk past him.
Cataclysm moved him to be more accessible and left that branch a dead end with three mobs in it.
In here the branch is still the reason to detour.

cards.subject: Maur Grimtotem
cards.tag: A body in a side tunnel
lines: A tauren corpse, and he was a diplomat sent by Magatha Grimtotem herself to make peace with the troggs.
He never came back out. A quest sends you to find him and search him.
Cataclysm removed him and left the tunnel empty. He is still down here.

cards.subject: Taragaman the Hungerer
cards.tag: The felguard in the lava hollow
lines: Everyone assumes the big demon runs the cult. He does not.
The leaders are Bazzalan and Jergosh. This one is expendable bait, placed to lure young Horde adventurers in to their death.
The first real demon most Horde players ever kill was put there to kill them.

cards.subject: Hidden Enemies
lines: Thrall tells a level fifteen the shape of the whole conspiracy: "our enemy is the Shadow Council."
At the end Neeru drops the mask, says the Council's schemes elsewhere must not suffer, and names Ashenvale.
Thrall answers that his spies will investigate. No quest was ever built on it. Twenty years, still hanging.

cards.subject: Zelemar the Wrathful
lines: Veterans remember a fifth name in this dungeon. He was added in patch 2.0.3, on the eve of The Burning Crusade.
There are four bosses in here and no eredar.
Anyone telling you otherwise is remembering a later game.

cards.subject: Bazzalan
lines: The actual last boss is a satyr — the only satyr in a place otherwise full of orcs, troggs and elementals.
He is on a ledge above Jergosh the Invoker. Groups kill Jergosh, call it done, and walk out having missed him standing over their heads.
Nothing in the game ever explains what he wanted.
